lineages.title: Hyperion Cantos
lineages.creator: Dan Simmons

divergence.label: The Nuclear Jihad
divergence.delta: Real: 2038 is twelve years from now; there is no Palestinian state, and no nuclear weapon has been used in war since 1945. Fiction: a Palestinian nation, won after a century of struggle, lasts about a month before a nuclear war destroys it, and a second diaspora begins that will last five hundred years.
divergence.note: The Cantos give most of their history as backstory inside the pilgrims' tales, in AD years, in the Hegemony's calendar or in local calendars. The earliest year stated that is not our history is the Nuclear Jihad of 2038, so the fork is there. Nothing earlier is dated; the Hawking drive and the TechnoCore's origins are not. The later calendar splits in two: the Hyperion books' numbers (Duré's 2732, Melio's 2739, the Big Mistake of '38) put the Fall at 2764, while the Endymion books' AD years put it at 2852 and call the disaster the Big Mistake of '08. This lineage follows the Hyperion reckoning throughout.

events.description: The first novel appears: seven pilgrims tell their stories on the way to the Time Tombs. It wins the 1990 Hugo Award, and The Fall of Hyperion follows in March 1990.

events.title: Endymion is published

events.note: Real-world publication (February 1996); The Rise of Endymion followed in 1997.
events.binWhy: A real-world publication date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: The Nuclear Jihad
events.description: A Palestinian state, won after a century of struggle, lasts about a month before the Nuclear Jihad of 2038 destroys it. Its people begin a second diaspora that lasts five centuries and ends on marginal desert worlds such as Mars, where the soldier Fedmahn Kassad is born.

sources.title: Hyperion Cantos Wiki: Timeline (archived) - dates with page references to Hyperion, Endymion and The Rise of Endymion

events.note: The year is stated in Kassad's tale in Hyperion (p. 133 of the 1995 edition, per the wiki timeline). It is the earliest dated event in the Cantos that is not our history, so it is the fork.
events.binWhy: A nuclear war destroys a nation and scatters its people.

facets.change: a month-old nation → a nuclear ruin and a second diaspora

events.title: Year zero of the Hegemony calendar
events.description: Hegemony Standard dating counts from this year. A human Hegemony of some kind is already in place before the Earth dies: the Consul later learns that the Big Mistake was planned by the TechnoCore and 'the fledgling government of the Hegemony'.

events.binWhy: A human government spanning worlds starts its own calendar.

facets.change: national governments → a Hegemony with its own calendar

events.title: The Big Mistake
events.description: A research team in Kiev creates a small black hole that falls to the centre of the Earth and begins eating it from the inside. The century of quakes that follows is remembered as the Bad Times. Much later it comes out that the TechnoCore arranged it.

sources.title: Hyperion Cantos Wiki: Timeline (archived) - dates with page references to Hyperion, Endymion and The Rise of Endymion

events.note: Hyperion and The Fall of Hyperion call it the Big Mistake of '38. The wiki fixes the century by counting Martin Silenus's life forward to the pilgrimage (526 years). The Endymion books call it the Big Mistake of '08, a contradiction Simmons never resolved. Old Earth was in fact hidden in the Magellanic Clouds, not destroyed, as The Rise of Endymion reveals.
events.binWhy: A man-made disaster destroys the planet that human civilisation stands on, and it does not recover.

facets.change: a living Earth → a planet being eaten from inside

events.title: The Hegira
events.description: Humanity leaves the dying Earth for the stars. Ships using the Hawking drive, a human invention, carry colonists to hundreds of worlds, each voyage costing years of time-debt, and the Hegemony's WorldWeb is later spun from those colonies.

events.note: Hyperion says 2739 is 457 years after the Hegira, which gives 2282. Emigration had begun earlier; the Ousters left Old Earth's system before this.
events.binWhy: Humanity founds colonies around other stars on a mass scale.

facets.change: one home world → hundreds of colonies

events.title: The death of Old Earth
events.description: A century after the Big Mistake the Earth is gone, apparently to rubble around the Moon. Among the last to leave is the twenty-year-old Martin Silenus, who will write the Cantos.

sources.title: Hyperion Cantos Wiki: Timeline (archived) - dates with page references to Hyperion, Endymion and The Rise of Endymion

events.title: The Shrike appears on Hyperion
events.description: About nine years after Sad King Billy's colonists found a City of Poets near the Time Tombs, people begin to die. The killer is the Shrike, a four-armed creature of blades that can step outside time and that comes from the Tombs, which are moving backwards through time. Billy evacuates the city, and a church grows up around the Shrike.
events.inUniverse: nine years after the City of Poets was founded (Hyperion)

events.title: Father Duré finds the cruciform
events.description: An exiled Jesuit, Paul Duré, finds the Bikura, the survivors of a lost colony on Hyperion. They are kept alive by cruciforms, parasites that rebuild the body after death at the cost of the mind. One grows into him.
events.inUniverse: 17 Thomasmonth 2732 AD, 589 Hegemony Standard (Duré's journal, Hyperion)

sources.title: Hyperion Cantos Wiki: Timeline (archived) - dates with page references to Hyperion, Endymion and The Rise of Endymion

events.title: The Time Tombs begin to open
events.description: With an Ouster swarm heading for Hyperion, seven pilgrims set out for the Tombs on a last pilgrimage to the Shrike: a priest, a soldier, a poet, a scholar with his daughter who is ageing backwards, a detective, a Templar and the Consul. Each has a reason to face the Shrike.

events.title: The Fall of the Farcasters
events.description: As the pilgrims reach the Time Tombs, an attack reaches the WorldWeb itself. It is blamed on the Ousters but made by the TechnoCore, the AIs that built the farcasters. CEO Meina Gladstone orders every farcaster destroyed, which cuts the Core out of human space and breaks a civilisation of hundreds of worlds that had lived one step apart.
events.inUniverse: The Fall (Hyperion reckoning 2764; Endymion reckoning 2852 AD)

sources.title: Hyperion Cantos Wiki: Timeline (archived) - dates with page references to Hyperion, Endymion and The Rise of Endymion

events.note: Hyperion reckoning: the scholar's daughter was 25 when her illness began in 2739, and she is a newborn as the pilgrims go down into the Tombs, which gives 2764. The Endymion books count years After the Fall (AF) and state their own AD years (Raul born 3099 AD = 247 AF; 3131 AD = 279 AF), which put the Fall at 2852 AD, 88 years later than the Hyperion books' own numbers allow. This lineage follows the Hyperion books' reckoning (Fall = 2764) and adds the Endymion books' AF counts to it.

events.description: Duré, briefly pope as Teilhard I, dies unexpectedly, and Lenar Hoyt is raised from the cruciform they shared and elected in his place. The Church offers resurrection to anyone who accepts the cruciform, and with its fleets it fills the space the Hegemony left, as the Pax. The cruciforms, it later turns out, come from the Core.

events.title: Aenea steps out of the Time Tombs
events.description: Aenea, the daughter of the detective Brawne Lamia and a machine-made copy of John Keats, walks out of the Tombs 274 years after she entered them at the age of twelve. The Pax is waiting to take her as an abomination. Raul Endymion, a Hyperion hunting guide sent by the ancient Martin Silenus, gets her away.
events.inUniverse: 274 After the Fall (3126 AD by Endymion)

events.title: Aenea's death and the Shared Moment
events.description: Aenea, who has been passing on a communion that frees people from the cruciform and lets them travel through the Void Which Binds, is arrested on Pacem, tortured and burned to death. At the moment she dies, her thoughts reach most of humanity through the Void, and a rising against the Pax and the TechnoCore follows.

events.note: Derived from Aenea's age: she comes out of the Tombs at twelve (274 AF), is sixteen when she sends Raul away, and is twenty-one when they meet again after a five-year time-debt, shortly before Pacem. That gives about 283 AF: 3047 here, c. 3135 by the Endymion books' numbers. The Endymion books count years After the Fall (AF) and state their own AD years (Raul born 3099 AD = 247 AF; 3131 AD = 279 AF), which put the Fall at 2852 AD, 88 years later than the Hyperion books' own numbers allow. This lineage follows the Hyperion books' reckoning (Fall = 2764) and adds the Endymion books' AF counts to it.

lineages.groupingNote: The archetype's theocratic and machine-haunted empire: a Hegemony of two hundred worlds joined by farcasters it does not understand, the AIs that built them and are feeding on it, and the Church that rises when the network is destroyed. It belongs here for its scale and its three-civilisation politics (Hegemony, Ousters, TechnoCore). Continuity: the four novels (Hyperion 1989, The Fall of Hyperion 1990, Endymion 1996, The Rise of Endymion 1997), dated on the Hyperion books' reckoning, with the Endymion books' After-the-Fall counts added to a Fall in 2764. By the Endymion books' own AD years, everything after the Fall would be 88 years later. Tier coverage: T3 for the two publications; T2 for the Nuclear Jihad, the Hegemony calendar, the Big Mistake and the Hegira (2038-2282); T1 for everything from the death of Old Earth (2338) to the Shared Moment (3047). No T4, because nothing before our own century is dated.

lineages.title: Babylon 5
lineages.creator: J. Michael Straczynski

divergence.label: Russia hands power to a strongman
divergence.delta: Real: in 2013 Russia had been under Vladimir Putin since 2000, with no Communist electoral victory and no civil war. Fiction: the Russians of 2013 are named on screen beside the Germans of the 1930s as a people who gave power to a tyrant, and tie-in canon adds an elected Communist government and a civil war.
divergence.inUniverse: Russia, 2013 (William Edgars in 'The Exercise of Vital Powers', 1997)
divergence.note: The series dates its own Earth history by the Common Era, so its years are ours. The earliest dated statement on screen that contradicts our history is Edgars's list in season 4, which runs Russia 1917, Germany 1939, Russia 2013, Iraq 2025 and France 2112. It is a single line and not the story's real hinge, which is the first contact with the Centauri in 2156; but it is the first year the fiction stops matching us, so the chain starts there. Earlier 21st-century entries in the tie-in chronology (an asteroid near-miss in 2011, for instance) do not contradict the real record.

sources.title: Reactor: Babylon 5 rewatch, 'The Exercise of Vital Powers' (Edgars cites Russia in 2013, Iraq in 2025, France in 2112)
The Babylon Project (wiki): Chronology (per the Historical Database in Across Time and Space)

ending.why: The series ends with the Shadows and Vorlons gone, the Interstellar Alliance founded and still holding twenty years later, and 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' shows that even after Earth burns in 2762 the Rangers rebuild it and humanity eventually becomes what the First Ones were.

events.title: Babylon 5: The Gathering airs
events.description: J. Michael Straczynski's pilot film airs on the PTEN network, setting up a space station, five ambassadors and a war ten years in the past.
events.note: A real-world publication event; the series proper began on 26 January 1994 and ran to 25 November 1998, with the fifth season on TNT.
events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: Babylon 5 begins its five-year run
events.description: The series premieres, planned from the start as a five-season novel for television with a beginning, middle and end.
events.note: A real-world publication event. 110 episodes over five seasons, followed by the spin-off Crusade (1999), The Lost Tales (2007) and the animated The Road Home (2023).
events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: Russia hands power to a strongman
events.description: In a list of peoples who gave power to tyrants because they were frightened, William Edgars names the Russians in 2013 alongside the Germans and the Russians of 1917. Later tie-in canon says a Communist government under a leader named Kolishnikov was elected, followed by civil war and twenty years as an economic colony of the West.

sources.title: Reactor: Babylon 5 rewatch, 'The Exercise of Vital Powers' (Edgars cites Russia in 2013, Iraq in 2025, France in 2112)

events.note: Stated on screen in 'The Exercise of Vital Powers' (season 4, written by Straczynski), which also names Iraq in 2025 and France in 2112. The detail of a Communist victory, Kolishnikov and the civil war comes from the tie-in novel Dark Genesis and is less certain. In our 2013 Russia already had a strongman, but he came to power in 2000 and faced no Communist electoral victory or civil war; this is the first dated point at which the show's Earth history is no longer ours.
events.binWhy: A leader is given power by election and fear and uses it to rule alone; the show uses it as a warning that people hand power over.

facets.change: a fearful electorate → a government given power

events.title: The Earth Alliance is founded after a third world war
events.description: A war that begins in 2080 between India, Pakistan and their allies over the Pacific Rim draws in the world and ends in 2084 at the cost of millions of lives. The next year the United Nations is dissolved and the regional blocs combine into the Earth Alliance, with its Senate in Geneva.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): World War III (2080-2084; Earth Alliance formed 2085)

events.note: The dates of the war and the Alliance's founding come from the Official Babylon 5 Magazine and the series' published chronology, not from dialogue; the show itself only ever refers to the Earth Alliance as long established. The real 2085 is sixty years away; the fiction reaches it through a non-nuclear world war.
events.binWhy: Independent powers unite under one charter, and it is the government everything later in the series is about.

facets.change: rival blocs after a world war → one Earth government

events.title: A Centauri ship arrives in the solar system
events.description: Humanity's first contact is with the Centauri, a declining empire who claim at first to run the galaxy and that humans are a lost colony of theirs. They trade Earth access to hyperspace, first by leasing time on alien jumpgates and then by selling the technology.
events.note: The exact date, 7 April 2156, is given in the tie-in novel Dark Genesis; the series establishes the Centauri as humanity's first contact and the source of its jump technology. The novel also has Earth's Alliance on the verge of breaking up just before, over the regulation of telepaths, and rescued by the contact.
events.binWhy: Humanity confirms and meets a non-human intelligence, and it opens the way to the stars.

facets.change: alone in the dark → a Centauri ship with a jumpgate to sell

events.title: The Psi Corps is founded
events.description: The Earth Alliance charters a single body to register, train and control its telepaths, who must join it, take sleeper drugs or be hunted. Its director reports to almost no one.
events.note: Date from Dark Genesis, the canon tie-in novel on the Corps' origins; the chronology has Earth scientists certifying telepathy in 2115 and a Metasensory Regulation Authority from 2117, which the Corps replaces. On screen the Corps is simply there, powerful and feared.
events.binWhy: A body is founded that will shape the Earth Alliance from inside: a guild of telepaths that is also their jailer and the state's secret instrument.

facets.change: unregistered telepaths → one corps that owns them

events.title: An Earth ship fires on the Minbari, and the Earth-Minbari War begins
events.description: An Earthforce expedition meets a Minbari cruiser that approaches with its gunports open, as a mark of respect, and opens fire, killing Dukhat, the leader of the Grey Council. The Minbari answer with a war of extermination that Earth cannot win.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2240s timeline (Earth-Minbari War, Battle of the Line)

events.note: Dated to July 2245 in the TV film In the Beginning and the series' chronology. Humanity loses nearly every battle for three years.
events.binWhy: A war between species begins, and it is a misunderstanding.

facets.change: a first meeting → a war of extermination

events.title: The Minbari surrender at the Battle of the Line
events.description: With Earth's last defences breaking, the Minbari capture an Earthforce pilot, discover that human souls are Minbari souls, and surrender without explanation. The reason stays secret for over a decade.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2240s timeline (Earth-Minbari War, Battle of the Line)

events.note: Dated to 2248 in the chronology; the surrender and its reason are shown in 'And the Sky Full of Stars', 'Points of Departure' and In the Beginning. Mars declares neutrality in the war the same year, and Earth's President announces the Babylon Project after the surrender.
events.binWhy: The enemy offers peace at the moment of victory; it is a truce with a secret inside it, not a decision on the battlefield.

facets.change: the edge of extinction → an unexplained surrender

events.title: Babylon 5 comes online
events.description: After four earlier stations are sabotaged or vanish, the fifth Babylon station opens in orbit of Epsilon III: five miles of metal holding a quarter of a million humans and aliens, and a council where the powers talk instead of fighting.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): Babylon 5 (station online 9 March 2256)

events.note: The wiki gives the station as online from 9 March 2256; the pilot is set in January 2257 and the series proper begins in 2258. Built by the Earth Alliance with Minbari backing.
events.binWhy: A permanent station is founded in space as a meeting ground; its purpose is diplomatic, but what it is, physically, is a settlement in orbit.

facets.change: wars between strangers → one station to talk in

events.title: President Santiago dies and Morgan Clark takes office
events.description: Earthforce One explodes over Io, killing the Earth Alliance president, and Vice-President Clark is sworn in on Earthforce Two. Evidence that it was an assassination vanishes on the way to Earth, and Clark's administration draws ever closer to the Psi Corps and to the Shadows.
events.note: Shown in 'Chrysalis', the season 1 finale; the date is given in the series' Historical Database. The same year the Narn-Centauri war begins and the Shadows return.
events.binWhy: A palace faction takes the state by murder and calls it a succession: the coup is hidden inside a tragedy.

facets.change: an elected president → his murderer's ally in his chair

events.title: Martial law, and Babylon 5 secedes from Earth
events.description: Clark declares martial law and has Earthforce bomb civilian targets on Mars. Mars, Proxima III, Orion VII and Babylon 5 declare independence, and the station beats off Clark's destroyers with Minbari help.
events.note: Martial law is dated to 9 April 2260 ('Point of No Return') and the secession to 14 April ('Severed Dreams'). The Shadow War is being fought at the same time.
events.binWhy: An armed revolt against a government turned tyranny, in which a station and three colonies take up arms against the capital.

facets.change: a loyal outpost → a rebel station

events.title: The Shadow War ends at Coriana VI
events.description: Sheridan's fleet refuses to let the Vorlons and Shadows fight their war through the younger races, and at Coriana VI both are sent beyond the Rim with the other First Ones. By November Sheridan's forces reach Earth, and Clark kills himself rather than surrender.
events.note: The Battle of Coriana VI ('Into the Fire') is dated to January 2261 and the end of the Earth Alliance Civil War ('Endgame') to November 2261; the Interstellar Alliance is proclaimed on 30 December. The year's three big events are merged; the decisive one is taken as the war's end.
events.binWhy: The war that shaped the galaxy is settled: the old powers leave, and the younger races are left to run it themselves.

facets.change: gods using the young as pawns → the young on their own

events.title: Earth joins the Interstellar Alliance
events.description: The alliance proclaimed at Babylon 5 on the last days of 2261 takes in the Earth Alliance under its new government, with Sheridan as its first president and the Rangers as its arm. For the first time the major powers and the non-aligned worlds are under one charter.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): Interstellar Alliance (formed 30 December 2261)
The Babylon Project (wiki): The Deconstruction of Falling Stars (records dated 2262, 2362, 2762, 3262 and a million years on)

events.note: The wiki dates the founding of the Interstellar Alliance to 30 December 2261 ('Rising Star'); 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' opens on a record dated 2 January 2262, reporting that Earth has decided to join. The event is filed under 2262 because 2261 already holds the end of the war.
events.binWhy: Independent powers unite under one charter; the ending the series was built towards.

facets.change: a council of rivals → one alliance of worlds

events.title: Sheridan goes beyond the Rim, and Babylon 5 is demolished
events.description: Twenty years after the end of the war, the Alliance's first president feels his borrowed life run out, says goodbye to his friends and flies alone to Coriana VI, where his ship is found empty. Soon after, Earthforce blows up the old station, its traffic gone.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): 2280s timeline (Sheridan's passing, January 2281)

events.note: 'Sleeping in Light', the series finale, set in January 2281; the wiki gives 14 January for Sheridan's departure.
events.binWhy: A ruler leaves and does not come back, and an era ends with the building that held it; his work has already become the Alliance.

facets.change: a founding president → an empty ship and a legend

events.title: The Great Burn
events.description: Five hundred years on, an Earth faction that resents the Alliance plans a surprise attack on the colonies; its rivals strike first, and the civil war that follows burns the Earth back to a pre-industrial world that remembers Sheridan as scripture.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): The Deconstruction of Falling Stars (records dated 2262, 2362, 2762, 3262 and a million years on)

events.note: Shown in 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' through a record dated 2 January 2762, the Alliance's 500th anniversary; the name and the scale of the destruction come from the episode's 3262 segment. Whether nuclear weapons were used is not stated.
events.binWhy: Weapons of war burn a civilisation's home world and kill on the scale that ends it; the Rangers spend centuries rebuilding.

facets.change: an alliance at five hundred → a burned Earth

events.title: Humanity leaves the Sun as beings of light
events.description: A million years after the Alliance began, the Sun is about to go nova. The last human on Earth, a being of pure energy in an encounter suit, sends the archive to New Earth and leaves as the Sun explodes.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): The Deconstruction of Falling Stars (records dated 2262, 2362, 2762, 3262 and a million years on)

events.note: The last segment of 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' is set a million years after 2262; the wiki dates it 1,002,262. Straczynski said humans and Minbari had by then reached an existence like the First Ones', and that the early nova was caused by someone opening jump points inside the Sun.
events.binWhy: Humanity has passed beyond anything a human being was, and leaves its birthplace as the Vorlons once did.

facets.change: a species in bodies → beings of light leaving a dying Sun

lineages.groupingNote: Far-future space opera: many species, a station at the centre of galactic politics, a war among ancient powers and a new interstellar union. The chain follows the television continuity (the five seasons and the TV films) as dated by the series' Historical Database and The Babylon Project wiki, with dates from the JMS-approved tie-in novels (Dark Genesis for 2156 and 2161) and the Official Magazine (2080-2085) where the show gives none; those carry medium confidence. Crusade and later spin-offs are left out. Tier coverage: T3 holds only the two release dates; T2 holds almost everything (2013-2281); T1 holds the far future of 'The Deconstruction of Falling Stars' (2762 and a million years on). T4 is empty because the series' Earth history is ours until the 21st century.

sources.title: The Babylon Project (wiki): Chronology (per the Historical Database in Across Time and Space)
The Babylon Project (wiki): 2240s timeline (Earth-Minbari War, Battle of the Line)
The Babylon Project (wiki): The Deconstruction of Falling Stars (records dated 2262, 2362, 2762, 3262 and a million years on)

lineages.title: Firefly
lineages.creator: Joss Whedon

divergence.label: The Alliance goes to war to unify the planets
divergence.delta: Real: 2506 is five centuries off and humanity has not left Earth. Fiction: Earth-That-Was was used up and abandoned generations earlier, a new star system has been terraformed and settled, and the Alliance of the central planets goes to war to bring the outer ones under its rule.
divergence.inUniverse: 2506-2511 (Firefly Wiki; the series itself dates only the war's end, six years before 2517)
divergence.note: The 'Verse is dated very sparsely. The series and film give one year, 2517, and one interval, six years back to Serenity Valley, plus River's age. The exodus from Earth-That-Was, which is where the fiction really parts from us, is never dated: Whedon's production memo for Serenity describes it without a year, and the Firefly Wiki's detailed 21st-century timeline is marked on the page as not all canon. Following this group's practice (Dune, Foundation), the fork is put at the first dated event of the fiction's own history, the start of the Unification War, and that start year is itself only the wiki's. The undated exodus is left out of the chain rather than given an invented year.

sources.title: Firefly Wiki: A Brief History of the Universe (Whedon's production memo for Serenity)
Firefly Wiki: Timeline (flagged on the page as partly non-canon)

ending.why: The Miranda recording is out and the Reaver fleet is broken, but the Alliance still rules, half the 'Verse thinks the broadcast is a hoax, and the resistance it started has not yet fought.

events.title: Seceded states open fire at Fort Sumter
events.description: South Carolina's militia bombards a federal fort in Charleston harbour, and the American Civil War begins between a central government and the states that have left it. Firefly's Unification War is modelled on it.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Fort Sumter (12-13 April 1861)

events.note: Real history. Whedon built the show on the American Civil War and its aftermath: a war between a central union and breakaway territories, and what became of the losers. The parallel is deliberately loose; the Browncoats' cause is independence from the centre rather than slavery.
events.binWhy: The original of the war the show retells: a state's own parts at war over whether they may leave it.

facets.change: a union → a union at war with its seceded states

events.title: The Battle of Gettysburg
events.description: Three days of fighting in Pennsylvania end with the Confederate army beaten and in retreat, and the war turns. Whedon conceived Firefly after reading Michael Shaara's novel about it, The Killer Angels.
events.note: Real history; the battle ran 1-3 July 1863. Wikipedia's Firefly article, citing Serenity: The Official Visual Companion, says Whedon developed the show after reading The Killer Angels and wanted to follow people who had fought on the losing side.
events.binWhy: A battle that turns a war, and the one from which the show's idea came.

facets.change: an invasion of the North → a beaten army in retreat

events.title: The Confederacy surrenders and Reconstruction begins
events.description: Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House, the South is occupied and reorganised, and many of the men who fought for it go west. Firefly's crew are these people five centuries on: veterans of the losing side, living on the frontier.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Appomattox Court House (9 April 1865)

events.note: Real history. Reconstruction ran from 1865 to 1877. Whedon's stated model for the show was the post-Civil War era of Reconstruction and the American Old West.
events.binWhy: A defeated power is occupied and dissolved into the victor, which is the situation Mal and Zoe live in after Serenity Valley.

facets.change: a breakaway republic → occupied territory and drifting veterans

events.title: Firefly premieres on Fox
events.description: Joss Whedon's series premieres on Fox, which airs its episodes out of order and cancels it that December with three of fourteen unaired.
events.note: A real-world publication event. The unaired episodes were shown later and the series found its audience on DVD.
events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: Serenity is released
events.description: Whedon's film continues the cancelled series and answers its central mystery: who River Tam is and what the Alliance did on Miranda.
events.note: A real-world publication event; the film premiered at the Edinburgh festival on 22 August and opened in North America on 30 September 2005. The story continued in Dark Horse comics, several co-written by Joss and Zack Whedon.
events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: The Alliance goes to war to unify the planets
events.description: The central planets, allied as the Union of Allied Planets, go to war against outer worlds that refuse to join them. The Independents, the 'Browncoats', are outnumbered and outgunned from the start.
events.note: The series never states when the war began. The Firefly Wiki gives it as 2506 to 2511, which fits the show's six-year gap after its end and a war of several years; no canonical source for the start year was found. The earlier history of the 'Verse, when Earth-That-Was was abandoned and the new system terraformed, is not dated in any canonical source.
events.binWhy: A war between the central government and the worlds that want out of it: a civil war fought between planets, like the one it copies.

facets.change: independent frontier worlds → a war for their annexation

events.title: The Independents are broken at Serenity Valley
events.description: On the planet Hera, seven weeks of fighting end when Independent High Command surrenders; the troops in the valley had been left to hold on, and die, while the terms were talked over. Sergeant Malcolm Reynolds, who survives, names his ship after the place.

sources.title: Firefly Wiki: Battle of Serenity Valley (May 2511)

events.note: The pilot opens on the battle and then jumps 'six years later' to 2517. The wiki dates the start of the battle to May 2511. It is taken as the end of the war, though not every engagement stops there.
events.binWhy: The battle that settles the war and ends the Independents' cause.

facets.change: a hard-pressed resistance → surrender and annexation

events.title: River Tam is taken into the Academy
events.description: A gifted fourteen-year-old from a rich core-world family goes to an Alliance school for the brightest children. It is a programme that cuts into her brain to turn her into a psychic weapon, and in the process she learns the government's worst secrets.

sources.title: Firefly Wiki: River Tam (born 2500; the Academy)

events.note: River is 17 in 2517, which places her birth in 2500; Simon says she went to the Academy at 14 and he spent two years trying to free her. Neither the series nor the film states the year of her entry; c. 2514 is derived from those ages.
events.binWhy: A person is chosen, by her gifts and by the state that wants to use them, and the future of the 'Verse later turns on what she knows.

facets.change: a gifted child → a weapon who knows too much

events.title: The truth about Miranda is broadcast to the 'Verse
events.description: The crew of Serenity find the planet Miranda, where the Alliance dosed a whole population with a chemical to make it docile: most simply lay down and died, and a tenth of a percent became the Reavers. Through Mr. Universe's relay they send the recording to every world.
events.note: Wikipedia sets both the series and the film in 2517, and the film follows the series by some months. The film does not date the Miranda experiment itself; it happened before the series, which already has Reavers in it. In our 2517 there is nothing to compare; the event is a state crime disclosed by those it was hidden from.
events.binWhy: What the government did and hid is made public by the people it tried to kill for knowing it.

facets.change: a buried experiment → a broadcast to every world

events.title: A new resistance forms around the Miranda broadcast
events.description: Eight months on, the 'Verse is split between people who think the broadcast was a hoax and people who believe it, and the Alliance has put a price on Reynolds's head. A Browncoat group calling itself the New Resistance wants him to lead it, while Operatives hunt his crew.

sources.title: Firefly Wiki: Serenity: Leaves on the Wind (set nine months after the film)

events.note: Serenity: Leaves on the Wind (Dark Horse, 2014, written by Zack Whedon) is set eight to nine months after the film. The film is in 2517, so 2518 is likely but not stated. The comic continues in later Dark Horse and Boom! series that are left out here.
events.binWhy: An armed resistance forms against those in power, started by the disclosure; it is still recruiting rather than fighting.

facets.change: a disclosed crime → a movement looking for a leader

lineages.groupingNote: Far-future space opera in the frontier mode: a settled star system, a central government that won a war of unification, and the losers scraping a living on its edge. The chain follows the series, the film Serenity and the Dark Horse comic Leaves on the Wind. The 'Verse gives very few dates (2517, six years back to 2511, River's age), so the fictional chain is short: the war's start (low confidence), Serenity Valley, River's recruitment and the Miranda broadcast and its aftermath. The minimum is filled with the real history Whedon built the show on: the American Civil War, Gettysburg and Reconstruction. Tier coverage: T4 for 1861-1865, T2 for the two releases only, T1 for every fictional event (2506-2518). T3 is empty because nothing the show draws on happens in the 20th century.

sources.title: Firefly Wiki: A Brief History of the Universe (Whedon's production memo for Serenity)

lineages.title: Dead Space
lineages.creator: Glen Schofield (creator); EA Redwood Shores / Visceral Games; remake by Motive Studio

divergence.label: New Horizons, the first colony on the Moon
divergence.delta: Real: nobody lives on the Moon, NASA's Artemis plans put a surface base in the 2030s at the earliest, and the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991. Fiction: by 2045 the United States and China have founded New Horizons, a permanent strip-mining colony on the Moon, while American and Soviet fleets go to war in the Bering Sea.
divergence.inUniverse: 2045: New Horizons founded as a Sino-US joint mining base (No Known Survivors, EA's 2008 promotional website; repeated in the Dead Space 3 Prima guide)
divergence.note: Dead Space dates in our calendar, so its years need no conversion. The fork is placed at the first dated thing that departs from the human record. The lore also says the Chicxulub impactor 66 million years ago was the Black Marker itself, which then nudged human evolution; that is a claim about a buried object nobody could see until 2214, so, following the convention the atlas uses for Mass Effect's Protheans, it is noted here rather than used as the fork. The 2045-2050 material comes from No Known Survivors, a 2008 promotional site whose events the later games still reference, which is why confidence is medium. Its 'Soviet Union' at war in 2045 implies an earlier, undated break with our 1991; no year can be given for it. The main-canon fork, if the promotional site is set aside, is the Black Marker's discovery in 2214.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: New Horizons Lunar Colony (founded 2045 as a Sino-US mining base)
Dead Space Wiki: Bering Sea conflict (US and Soviet Union, 2045-2050)

ending.why: At the end of Dead Space 3: Awakened (2514) the Brethren Moons have reached Earth, the Unitologist Circle has already gutted EarthGov's defences, and Isaac and Carver's hails are answered only by necromorph noise.

events.title: Dead Space is released
events.description: EA Redwood Shores releases Dead Space in North America on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, with the Windows version a week later. It is set in 2508 aboard a mining ship overrun after the discovery of an alien Marker.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Dead Space (2008 video game) (North American release 13 October 2008; set in 2508)

events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: Dead Space 3 is released
events.description: Visceral Games releases the last numbered game, which explains the Markers' origin on Tau Volantis; its Awakened episode follows in March and ends with the Brethren Moons at Earth. The series then sits dormant until the 2023 remake of the first game.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Dead Space 3 (North American release 5 February 2013; Awakened DLC March 2013)

events.binWhy: A real-world release date, not a moment in the story.

events.title: New Horizons is founded on the Moon
events.description: The United States and China open a joint strip-mining base on the Moon, the first permanent settlement off Earth, and it grows rich on helium-3 during an energy crisis at home. Five centuries later it is a filthy lunar metropolis, and the place Isaac Clarke goes to hide.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: New Horizons Lunar Colony
Dead Space Wiki: Earth (21st-century history: energy crisis, New Horizons, the Bering Sea conflict)

events.note: The year comes from No Known Survivors, EA's 2008 promotional website, and is repeated in the Dead Space 3 Prima guide; the games themselves show the colony only in 2511-2514. In our 2045 the Moon has no permanent residents and lunar helium-3 mining is a proposal.
events.binWhy: A permanent base is founded on the Moon.

facets.change: an empty Moon → a Sino-US mining colony

events.title: The Battle of the Bering Sea
events.description: After a Soviet force seizes the crew of an American freighter in the Kara Sea in 2045, the US Third Fleet fights the Red Banner Northern and Pacific Fleets off the Chukchi Peninsula in 2047 and again in 2050. The war ends with Soviet forces holding the peninsula.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: Bering Sea conflict (Kara Sea Hostage Crisis 2045; naval battles 2047 and 2050)

events.note: Known only from maps and a genealogy report in the No Known Survivors promotional site, so its standing in the canon is thin. 2047 is the first of the two dated fleet battles; the hostage crisis that opens the conflict is 2045 and is folded in here because the colony takes that year. That the enemy is 'the Soviet Union' in 2045 is itself a break with our history that the lore never dates.
events.binWhy: Two great powers fight a naval war over the Arctic.

facets.change: a hostage crisis → fleet battles off Chukotka

events.title: The Black Marker is found in the Chicxulub crater
events.description: A team including the geophysicist Michael Altman, working with the military of the Sovereign Colonies, raises a twisted alien monolith from the crater under the old Gulf of Mexico. It seems to give off limitless energy; it also brings dementia, suicide and the dead getting up again, and the government buries the details.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Dead Space: Martyr (novel set in 2214)

events.note: Stated in Dead Space 3's briefing and in the 2010 novel Martyr, which is set in 2214. The lore holds that this object was the Chicxulub impactor itself; in our history the crater is the scar of an asteroid, and the atlas treats the Marker's presence as invisible until the day it is dug up.
events.binWhy: A technology left by a non-human intelligence is found and studied.

facets.change: an impact crater → an alien artefact that seems to give limitless energy

events.title: Altman is killed, and Unitology is born
events.description: Altman makes the Marker public against the government's wishes and is assassinated. A church founded in his name teaches that the Marker holds the secret of death and rebirth, and it grows into the largest religion in human space, rich enough to own a stake in the company that mines the worlds.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: Michael Altman (died c. 15 March 2215)
EA: The World and History of Dead Space (archived; Unitology founded 2215)

events.note: The date of death is from the in-game Unitology logs; EA's own narrative page for the 2023 remake gives the founding year as 2215. Martyr suggests the church was built around Altman against his will.
events.binWhy: A church is founded that will shape human space for three centuries.

facets.change: a murdered scientist → a church in his name

events.title: The Sovereign Colonies build their own Markers
events.description: Eighty years after the Black Marker, government scientists reverse-engineer it into copies, the Red Markers, hoping for an end to the resource crisis. The copies are planted in secret on remote worlds such as Aspera, Kreemar and Aegis VII, and every test site is overrun by the reanimated dead.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: Timeline (2294-2311: Red Markers replicated and tested)

events.note: Dead Space 3's Serrano briefing says 'eighty years after' the 2214 discovery, which gives 2294 by arithmetic; the covert deployments and outbreaks are spread over the following years and told in Dead Space: Catalyst and the Tau Volantis logs.
events.binWhy: An alien power source is copied and switched on as an energy technology.

facets.change: one alien original → human-made copies on secret worlds

events.title: The expedition to Tau Volantis
events.description: The Sovereign Colonies Armed Forces follow the Markers' 'master signal' to a frozen planet beyond the colonies and land a covert expedition. Under the ice lie the remains of an alien civilisation that built Markers two million years ago and froze its own world to stop what they started.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: Timeline (29 August 2311, initial drop zone on Tau Volantis)

events.note: The date is from an in-game log in Dead Space 3. The expedition was a gamble to end the Resource Wars and the Secession War with Marker energy; it is also where the Colonies' council classified the Markers as a 'Class 5' first-contact scenario.
events.binWhy: A first mission is sent to a distant, unexplored alien world.

facets.change: a signal's source → a frozen alien graveyard

events.title: Scenario Five, and the end of the Sovereign Colonies
events.description: Judging the Markers an extinction-level threat, the Sovereign Colonies order everything about them destroyed. On Tau Volantis General Mahad's loyalists execute the science staff, wreck the fleet and mine the orbit before Mahad kills himself. The purge leaves the government unable to fight its civil war, it collapses, and an Earth-centred EarthGov takes its place.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: Timeline (18 June 2314, Scenario Five completed)
EA: The World and History of Dead Space (archived; EarthGov founded 2314)

events.note: The purge is shown in Dead Space 3's prologue; EA's narrative page for the remake dates EarthGov's founding to 2314. The purge also buries the Black Marker somewhere in the galaxy, which is why the Markers are a rumour again two centuries later.
events.binWhy: A government has its own scientists killed and its own records destroyed.

facets.change: a research programme → executed scientists and a buried secret

events.title: Titan is cracked, and the Ishimura is launched
events.description: Gravity-tether mining breaks up Saturn's moon Titan, and the Concordance Extraction Corporation launches the USG Ishimura, the first 'planet cracker', with one of the first ShockPoint faster-than-light drives. Whole worlds are fed into ships, the Resource Wars end, and the station built on Titan's last shard becomes the Sprawl.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: Planet Cracking (Titan cracked around 2446; Ishimura built 2446)
Dead Space Wiki: Titan Station (commissioned c. 2446)

events.note: In-game sponsored articles give 2446 for the Ishimura; the Titan harvest is dated only to 'the 2440s', and EA's remake page says the Resource Wars were raging 'by the early 2440s'. The Ishimura's 'over sixty years' of service by 2508 agrees.
events.binWhy: A new industrial process, mining by cracking whole worlds, is put to work.

facets.change: starving colonies → whole worlds mined for ore

events.title: The Ishimura at Aegis VII
events.description: Miners cracking Aegis VII, a restricted world, dig up a Red Marker the old government left there, and the Ishimura takes it aboard for the Church. Insomnia and murder follow, then the dead of the colony and the ship rise as necromorphs; the engineer Isaac Clarke arrives to repair a silent ship and finds almost no one alive.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Dead Space (2008 video game) (set in 2508)

events.note: The year is stated by the game and by EA's remake page ('It is now 2508'). Isaac returns the Marker to its pedestal and the planet's fragment falls back on the colony, but EarthGov recovers the derelict Ishimura within a month.
events.binWhy: An alien signal turns the dead into something else, and the outbreak kills a colony and a ship.

facets.change: an illegal mining colony → a ship of the reanimated dead

events.title: Unitologists open the Sprawl to the necromorphs
events.description: EarthGov has built a new Marker in a secret lab on Titan Station, a city of over a million. Unitologists sabotage the lab's sector and trick an engineer into opening the tubes to the public sector, the outbreak spreads, and the station is destroyed by its own reactors after Isaac destroys the Marker.

sources.title: Dead Space Wiki: Titan Station (population over one million; destroyed 7 February 2511)

events.note: The February date is from the Dead Space: Sabotage tie-in and in-game video logs; the game itself states only 2511. The disaster turns the public against EarthGov and opens a three-year Unitologist insurgency.

events.description: Isaac and his allies reach Tau Volantis and find that the Markers exist to make 'Brethren Moons', planet-sized masses of flesh that harvest whole species. They destroy the one that wakes there, but more of them are already in Earth orbit, and no one on Earth or the Moon answers.

Dead Space Wiki: Earth (Brethren Moon invasion, 2514)

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs in far-future space opera: a human interstellar polity of colonies and mining worlds reached by ShockPoint drive, running on corporate extraction and a church, with an alien intelligence far older than humanity at its centre; unusually for the group, no living alien civilisation is ever met. lineages.creator: Bungie

divergence.label: Something that is 'neither holy nor unholy' meets two boys outside Assumption, Illinois
divergence.delta: Real: in 1938 Assumption is a small Illinois town on Route 51 and nothing comes down the road but traffic. Fiction: III of the Nine, a higher-dimensional intelligence, appears to thirteen-year-old Louis Yero and his brother Ben, the first dated moment of a hidden twentieth century that a secret US agency, the Department of External Observation, will spend decades studying and concealing.
divergence.inUniverse: Assumption, Illinois, 1938 (lore book Assumption, Destiny 2: Monument of Triumph, June 2026)
divergence.note: Destiny's main story carries no calendar at all, but lore added in 2025-2026 (The Edge of Fate's DEO documents and the Monument of Triumph lore books) gives it a dated, secret twentieth century, and the earliest dated departure in it is this 1938 encounter; the year is printed as a section heading. The Traveler's far older history (the Precursors, the Hive, the Vex) happens off Earth and is left out, as the atlas does for Mass Effect's Protheans. Everything after the DEO is derived, and every derived year is low or medium confidence: the Traveler reaches Mars 'in what we know as the late 21st century' (Game Informer, 2015), placed here at 2080; the Golden Age is 'centuries-long'; and the first game is set 'about 700 years in the future' (Wikipedia; from Bungie's 2012 leaked story document), taken as 2014 + 700 = 2714. From there Bungie's live game keeps in-universe time roughly in step with real time (Destinypedia dates the Witness's last campaign to 4 June, the release day of The Final Shape), so later beats are placed at release year + 700. The DEO's own 1960s memo, which expects the object X0192 to arrive in '50-60 years', would put the Traveler in the 2010s or 2020s instead; the two statements are not reconciled in the canon.

sources.title: Game Informer: What's Going On In Destiny's Story, Anyway? (2015; the Traveler arrives in the late 21st century)

ending.why: The Witness is dead and the Traveler saved, but when Bungie ended development in June 2026 III of the Nine was dead, Earth's chemistry was changing, and the Nine's prophecy of extinction was unanswered, with the Fate Saga cut short.

events.title: III of the Nine meets Louis Yero
events.description: Out of fuel on a highway in Illinois, two brothers meet a wavering figure that calls itself their mother and invites a question 'before death hastens me from this moment'. Louis is knocked unconscious; nearly thirty years later the same beings will pull him out of time to be their emissary.
events.note: The year is the lore book's own section heading. Nothing outside the brothers records it; it is the first of the hidden twentieth-century events Bungie added to the canon in 2026, a year before the franchise's content ended.
events.binWhy: An ordinary boy is drawn into the story of the Nine.

facets.change: a boy on a highway → a boy the Nine have marked

events.title: The Department of External Observation
events.description: A US agency in Chicago charged with extraterrestrial anomalies hires Yero as a linguist for alien translation, and his first case is a USS Hornet from another timeline that has appeared on the Pine Ridge Reservation. Its contact protocol runs 'observe, connect, conceal, conform, comply, return', and it also studies an energy weapon it suspects in the Kennedy assassination.

sources.title: Destinypedia: Lodi (DEO linguist from 1960; the Pine Ridge Hornet)
Destinypedia: Timelost DEO Documents (the Dealey Plaza memo)

events.note: The DEO's founding is undated; 1960 is the first year the lore places it at work. Its Dealey Plaza memo finds 'no conclusive link' between recovered alien weaponry and the 1963 assassination, so no change to that event is charted.
events.binWhy: A secret agency hides contact with the extraterrestrial from the public.

facets.change: anomalies in the field → anomalies in a vault

events.date: 1962 (first dated reference; the incident itself is undated)
events.title: The Diablerets suits
events.description: The DEO has recovered three intact alien survival suits from 'the Diablerets incident' in the Swiss Alps, with a silicone-based micro-organism still in their tubes. Departments fight over them, and by 1966 their reverse-engineering has produced public patents and a DARPA weapons programme.

sources.title: Destinypedia: Lore:Recovered Materials, Old Chicago (Magnetic Audiotape, 1962; Pocket Notebook, 1966)

events.note: A 1962 tape discusses the suits as already recovered, so the incident is earlier and undated. Destinypedia compares the DEO's handling of it to Roswell.
events.binWhy: Technology left by a non-human intelligence is recovered and taken apart.

facets.change: an alien crash site → suits on the workbench

events.title: The DEO images X0192
events.description: A DEO briefing flags an 'unidentified celestial body', spherical and abnormally regular, moving towards the Sun with an estimated arrival in fifty to sixty years: the Traveler. In 1966 the Nine take the mathematician Nella Davis and Louis Yero through 'strange matter', and the director swears to bring them back.

sources.title: Destinypedia: Timelost DEO Documents (the X0192 memo)

events.note: The memo carries no year; it sits among Yero's papers from his DEO years (1960-1966) and just before his disappearance, which the 1966 memoranda date, so it is filed at 1966 at low confidence. Nella Davis is later revealed to be Ikora Rey before she became a Guardian. The memo's 50-60 year estimate conflicts with the late-21st-century arrival used below.
events.binWhy: An astronomical discovery: an artificial sphere is heading for the solar system.

facets.change: an empty sky → a sphere on its way

events.title: Project BLUE DOOR opens a tear into another dimension
events.description: Reactivated to follow the missing pair, a mothballed DEO project opens a 15-centimetre hole into a place so full of strange matter that it turns the lab's equipment to iron filings. In 1968 Director Moffat steps through after a colleague whose organs are turned to metal; he comes back, and shuts the effort down.

sources.title: Destinypedia: Lore:Recovered Materials, Old Chicago (Introduction Letter, 1967; Magnetic Audiovisual Tape, 1968; Torn Journal Page, 12 December 1968)

events.note: Each lore entry carries its year. The 1968 tape records something on the other side answering the director in a patchwork of animal calls and human voices.
events.binWhy: A passage to another dimension is made.

facets.change: a mothballed project → a hole in the world

events.title: Ares One meets the Traveler on Mars
events.description: The first crewed flight to Mars, a US, Chinese and Russian mission under Commander Jacob Hardy, lands by hand after an engine fault and walks up a ridge to see the Traveler making it rain on the desert. It has already remade Mercury, Venus and the moons of Jupiter, and it offers humanity the solar system.

sources.title: Destinypedia: Ares One (the first crewed flight to Mars)
Ishtar Collective: Ghost Fragment: Human (Hardy's pre-launch log)
Game Informer: What's Going On In Destiny's Story, Anyway? (late 21st century)

events.note: No year is given in the games. Game Informer's 2015 story guide says 'the late 21st century'; 2080 is a placement inside that range, not a canon date. Hardy's log uses today's vocabulary (a Hohmann window, MREs, a fourteen-month transfer), which fits a crewed Mars programme only a little beyond ours.
events.binWhy: Humanity meets a non-human intelligence face to face.

facets.change: a visitor watched from afar → a partner that gives us the planets

events.title: The Golden Age
events.description: Fifty years after first contact, Hardy, now ninety, writes that humanity lives on the worlds the Traveler touched. Colonies spread from the Moon's Ocean of Storms to Freehold on Mars, the Ishtar Collective studies Vex ruins on Venus, lifespans lengthen, Clovis Bray builds the Exos, and the Warminds guard the system.

sources.title: Destinypedia: Golden Age (Hardy at ninety, fifty years after the Traveler's discovery)

events.note: The fifty-year interval is canon (Ghost Fragment: Human 4); the year inherits the low confidence of the Ares One placement. The Golden Age itself is 'centuries-long' and its milestones are undated, so they are gathered here rather than invented one by one.
events.binWhy: A civilisation at its peak, before the fall.

facets.change: one planet → a terraformed solar system

events.title: The Collapse
events.description: The Darkness arrives, the colonies fall, and humanity is driven back to Earth; the Traveler makes a last stand and falls silent over the place that becomes the Last City. A Dark Age of warlords follows, until Ghosts begin raising the dead as Guardians.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Destiny (video game) (the Traveler's appearance 'centuries before'; set about 700 years in the future)

events.note: Undated in the canon. It is bracketed by a late-21st-century first contact followed by a Golden Age of 'at least a few centuries', and by a Dark Age and City Age that Destinypedia estimates lasted at least four centuries before a first game set around 2714; both brackets meet near 2300. Treat the year as a placement, not a date.
events.binWhy: An outside force breaks a solar-system civilisation and it never comes back.

facets.change: a solar-system civilisation → one city under a silent god

events.title: A Ghost raises the Guardian
events.description: In the ruins of the Cosmodrome in Old Russia a Ghost resurrects a long-dead stranger as a Guardian, a warrior of the Traveler's Light. Within the year the new Guardian breaks the Vex's Black Garden and kills the Hive god Crota, and, in the Taken War that follows, his father Oryx.

The Register: Bungie details Destiny (2012; 'seven hundred years from now in the Last City')

events.binWhy: A person is chosen, by resurrection, as the one the story's future turns on.

facets.change: a corpse in the Cosmodrome → the Traveler's champion

events.date: c. 2717 ('two years after the Taken War')

sources.title: Destinypedia: Traveler ('two years after the Taken War')

events.title: The Witness is destroyed inside the Traveler
events.description: The Witness, the Darkness's intelligence, tries to calcify the Last City into its 'Final Shape'. Guardians and a coalition of former enemies follow it into the Pale Heart inside the Traveler and kill it; Cayde-6 gives his Light to save Ghost, and the city releases paper lanterns.

sources.title: Destinypedia: Timeline (the Witness's defeat; the Echoes)

events.note: The end of the ten-year Light and Darkness Saga. The year is the release year plus the 700-year anchor; Destinypedia dates the campaign by release days, which is the only basis for keeping story time in step with real time.

lineages.groupingNote: Belongs in far-future space opera: a solar-system civilisation lost in a Collapse, a Last City of resurrected knights under a silent god, alien empires (Cabal, Hive, Vex, Eliksni) and a war of Light against Darkness. The chain follows Bungie's canon as told in the games, the Grimoire and the lore books and catalogued by Destinypedia and the Ishtar Collective, through Monument of Triumph (June 2026). Only the 1938-1968 lore is dated; every later year is derived and marked low or medium. franchiseStatus is dormant because content development ended in June 2026, though Bungie said in September 2026 it would restore removed content as a foundation for new Destiny stories. Tiers: T4 is empty (the Traveler's ancient history happens off Earth and is left out); T3 holds the DEO's secret century, 1938-1967; T2 holds the releases, first contact and the Golden Age; T1 holds the Collapse and the City Age, around 2300 and 2714-2724.
